edits.old: The coefficient of the insertion grows as $1$, $|y|$, $|y|^2$ for constant, linear and quadratic vector fields or Killing spinors, and the two adjacent edges decay as $|y|^{-3}$ each (one derivative, Proposition \ref{prop:c3-P});
edits.new: On a cycle the terms of $S^{(1)}(x)$ with both legs on components of the propagator are $(v.A,A^*)$ for even $x$, with $v.A=L_vA+\tfrac14(\operatorname{div}v)A|_{W_{\mathbb R}^\perp}$ (Definition \ref{def:c7-vdot}), and $-(\Gamma(\epsilon(y),\lambda),A^*)$ for odd $x$, $\epsilon(y)=\xi+\rho(y)\eta$. The $A^*|_V$ leg meets an $A^*|_V\otimes c$ component and the $\lambda$ leg a $\lambda\otimes\lambda$ component, both of order $|y|^{-3}$; the $A$ leg meets an $A\otimes A$ component, of order $|y|^{-2}$ (Proposition \ref{prop:c3-P}). A vector field of degree $k$ enters through the derivative along $v$, of order $|y|^k$ acting on the $A\otimes A$ component, and through $dv$ and $\operatorname{div}v$, of order $|y|^{k-1}$, so the insertion is of order $|y|^{k-6}$; a Killing spinor of degree $g$ gives $|y|^{g-6}$;

edits.label: prop:c8-Tsafe (proof, arity two and K_b)
edits.old: for $(\xi,\eta)$ the two orientations traverse the $\lambda$ edge in opposite directions and their leading terms cancel. For $K_b$ the product is of order $|y|^{-4}$ with a nonzero average over the sphere, and $\int_{|y|^2<T}|y|^{-4}d^4y$ grows as $\pi^2\log T$.
edits.new: for $(\xi,\eta)$ the two orientations traverse the $\lambda$ edge in opposite directions and their leading terms cancel. For two floating even insertions the $A\otimes A$ edge between them carries both derivatives and is of order $|y|^{-4}$, the two $A^*|_V\otimes c$ edges are of order $|y|^{-3}$, and the two orientations of the chain enter with opposite signs, so their leading terms cancel. For $K_b$ the product is of order $|y|^{-4}$ with a nonzero average over the sphere; this term comes from the antisymmetric part of $dv$ acting on $A|_V$, while on $A|_{W_{\mathbb R}^\perp}$ the leading terms of the derivative along $v$ and of $\tfrac14\operatorname{div}v$ cancel. $\int_{|y|^2<T}|y|^{-4}d^4y$ grows as $\pi^2\log T$; $T\partial_T$ of the scalar integral of the composite line tends to $-\tfrac{3}{16\pi^2}b$, and with the fibre factors $2(-,-)^{-1}$ of $A\otimes A$ and $-(-,-)^{-1}$ of $A^*|_V\otimes c$ (Proposition \ref{prop:c8-twocomp}) it gives the coefficient $\tfrac{3}{8\pi^2}$ of the cut tree.
